messages.author: d88de118c479e0b6
messages.subject: HDL - NA in covariance
parts:
Hi all,

I am running into an issue where a certain trait produces NAs in the sampling covariance ($V) matrix in High Definition Likelihood.



I am essentially trying to replicate the GUT factor from this preprint, but the primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) trait causes the entire sampling covariance matrix to turn into NaNs. There is some missingness (~2.5%) but other two traits Crohn's Disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) have close to 3.5% missingness and still work fine on their own or with other traits. And from what I understand, HDL is robust to missingness and produces more conservative heritability estimates as missingness grows (up to 5% by author's testing).

I also noticed that on the covariance matrix ($S) PSC has 0 on the diagonal. Does that have something to do with the issue? Unfortunately HDL doesn't seem to have logs or error messages.

Regards,

Jeff

messages.author: d88de118c479e0b6
messages.subject: Re: HDL - NA in covariance
parts:
Hi Michel,

Sorry I dropped off on this.

For anyone else running into this problem, when I reran it in original HDL, I found that this is an error that happens when HDL finds heritability of 0 (in this case, PSC). It makes sense that $V outputs NA and $S contains 0. Might be worth adding an error message pointing out phenotypes with 0 heritability so they can be removed in the next run, and/or removing those traits automatically with a log message indicating so?

Regards,

Jeff
